name: TX-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Menefee running with large fundraising and outside support
Republican opponent has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 99%
model.rationale: The D+29 partisan lean, Menefee's incumbency and roughly $3.6 million raised against an opponent with no reported fundraising all point to a lopsided Democratic hold, and markets agree at 99%. No polls or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays moderately wide, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Menefee would be the first sign of movement, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-18 is a heavily Democratic Houston-area seat with a 29-point Democratic partisan lean. Incumbent Christian Menefee, first elected in a special election, is running for a full term and has raised about $3.6 million, backed by roughly $7 million in outside support and no recorded opposition spending. Republican Ronald Whitfield has no reported fundraising or cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals: the district lean, incumbency, and the large financial imbalance. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 99 percent. The expected margin is about 29 points, consistent with the seat's baseline, with residual uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of competition.
